Operator:  
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q2 FY2025 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one one on your telephone keypad followed by your name and affiliation. There will be a brief pause while registration is processed. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q2 FY2025 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Lisa Wong, CTO; and David Kim, Chief Revenue Officer.  

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of federal securities laws. Actual results may differ materially due to a variety of risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-Q and 10-K, for a complete discussion of these factors.  

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.  

Sarah Chen:  
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q2 FY2025. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our CloudForge Fusion AI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.  

Our focus this quarter was on five key areas: next quarter ARR guidance, MRR trends, NRR performance, full-year revenue guidance, and churn analysis. These metrics highlight the strength of our land-and-expand model and our ability to deliver value in a resilient SaaS market. Mike will provide detailed color on these shortly, but at a high level, we're seeing accelerating growth fueled by AI adoption and enterprise expansions.  

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.  

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss the financials in more detail.  

Mike Patel:  
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $320 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 80%, and operating income was $50 million.  

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong at over $600 million, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.  

Turning first to our MRR trends, which continue to be the cornerstone of our SaaS financial health here at CloudForge. I'm pleased to report that ending MRR reached $45.2 million at the end of Q2 FY2025, marking a robust 28% year-over-year increase from $35.1 million in Q2 FY2024. Sequentially, we delivered 8.2% quarter-over-quarter growth, accelerating from the 7.1% we saw in Q1. This outperformance against our guided range of 25-27% YoY underscores the resilience of our land-and-expand model in a macro environment where enterprise IT budgets remain selective, much like we've seen across peers such as Snowflake and Databricks during their post-hype stabilization phases.  

To break it down, new logo MRR contributed $4.8 million, or about 60% of the sequential increase, reflecting wins from our refreshed product-led growth motion in the mid-market. Existing customer expansions added another $2.1 million, driven by AI upsells, while churn impacts were minimal at under $0.9 million. Cohort-wise, our FY2024 signings are tracking at 125% NRR already, validating our focus on high-ACV enterprise deals.  

Next, let's discuss our NRR performance, which remains a cornerstone of our SaaS flywheel and a strong indicator of product stickiness and customer love. For Q2 FY2025, we delivered dollar-based NRR of 114%, up slightly from 112% in Q1 and up significantly year-over-year from 105% in Q2 FY2024. This positions us in line with top-tier peers like Snowflake around 108% and above the industry median of 102%, as noted in recent Bessemer Venture Partners' State of the Cloud surveys. On a cohort basis, our 12-month trailing NRR for customers onboarded in FY2024 now stands at 118%, reflecting the compounding power of our land-and-expand motion.  

Breaking it down by key drivers: expansion continues to be our growth engine at 25 percentage points, up from 22 points in Q1 and driving roughly 70% of our total NRR lift. This is fueled by adoption of our new AI Copilot module—our generative AI layer integrated natively with our core collaboration platform—which saw 28% penetration among eligible enterprise customers, adding an average of $45K in ARR per upsell. It's akin to Salesforce's Einstein or Workday's AI innovations, where customers layer on predictive analytics for workflow automation, yielding sticky economics with 95% renewal rates post-adoption. Seat expansions contributed another 8 points, especially in mid-market amid hybrid work trends similar to Zoom or Asana. Cross-sell into our security add-on suite rose 35% quarter-over-quarter as CISOs prioritize zero-trust amid ransomware threats. Regionally, US expansion hit 28 points with Fortune 500 cohorts like a major financial services firm expanding from 5,000 to 12,000 seats via ServiceNow API integrations. EMEA matched at 27 points with GDPR-compliant AI features in regulated verticals, while APAC was at 20 points due to data sovereignty issues in Japan and India, which we're tackling with localized edge computing.  

Contraction improved to 11 points, a 200 basis point gain from Q1's 13 points, as we lap pandemic-era deals. This affects about 9% of our base, mainly cost-sensitive SMBs under high interest rates—echoing Bessemer's average of 10-12%. Mitigators include our ML-driven dynamic pricing engine offering tailored bundles, cutting downgrade risk by 15%, and QBRs covering 92% of $10M+ ARR cohorts with ROI dashboards showing 25% faster decision cycles. North America had the lowest at 9 points thanks to enterprise stickiness, EMEA 12 points from FX and Nordic energy softness, and APAC 14 points from SEA telco rationalization post-5G, though NPS improved 8 points to 62.  

Gross dollar churn held at 4%, flat sequentially and down from 5.5% YoY—below the 7-8% SaaS average for enterprise players like HubSpot or Monday.com. This means 2.1% logo churn, with 96%+ cohort retention at 24 months. Non-renewals clustered in small EMEA retail logos hit by inflation, but win-back campaigns via freemium reclaimed 40%. Macro pressures like inflation and delayed budgets persist per KeyBanc surveys, but we're countering with 'Forge Forward' bundling Copilot with unlimited API calls at 20% premium, and seat-based consumption pilots mirroring ServiceTitan, eyeing 120% NRR in FY2026. We expect Q3 NRR at 115-118%, with expansion to 27 points as AI hits 35% adoption. Our 98% gross retention ex-downgrades builds a durable moat.  

Building on that, let's dive into our churn analysis. In Q2, logo churn was 6.8% annualized, down 220 basis points YoY from 9.0% and below the 8-10% peer median per Bessemer. Dollar-based gross revenue churn was 4.2% annualized, versus 6.1% last year, supporting 118% NRR with 28% expansion from upsells like our AI Resource Optimizer at 35% adoption.  

Primary drivers from our Gainsight-integrated win/loss analysis, tagging 95% of events: macroeconomic pressures at 35%, especially mid-market ($100K-$500K ARR) where 42% cited budgets amid inflation, mirroring Asana and Monday.com. Competitive displacement 28%, with Salesforce's Slack/Tableau CRM taking 15% in sales ops, Smartsheet in SMBs, and Atlassian Jira Align in EMEA PPM overlaps. Product/onboarding gaps 22%, with implementation at 45 days (up from 38) and feature misses like OKR tracking versus Ally.io. Regional/contractual 15%, APAC at 9.2% from FX and Japan timing, EMEA GDPR audits at 8%, versus NA 5%, plus pre-pandemic contract normalizations. Sequentially improving from Q1's 7.5% logo churn, trending down 150 bps over three quarters, though Q3 may test 7.0-7.5% if macro persists.  

Our mitigation via $25M 'Churn Fortress' initiative: CS team up 40% to 250, 7:1 ratio for >$1M ARR, Renewal Bootcamps yielding 94% renewals and 22% at-risk reduction. ForgePredict ML model on Snowflake/Databricks uses 200+ signals for 88% accuracy, automating Braze nudges that rescued 15% ($4.2M NRR add). AutoPilot onboarding with Slack/Teams/Jira integrations cuts time-to-value to 21 days, Q3 betas for OKR/ESG from VoC. APAC local billing (65%) and NTT partnerships dropped churn 300 bps; EMEA GDPR dashboard. FlexScale usage pricing stems 18% budget churn, targeting 14-month CAC payback. This drives Rule of 50 score of 153 (35% ARR growth +118% NRR), guiding FY25 logo churn to 6.0-6.5% and NRR to 120%+.  

Now, on full-year revenue guidance for FY2025 ending January 31, 2026, we're raising it to $1.28 billion to $1.32 billion, or 26% to 30% YoY growth from FY2024's $1.015 billion. This lifts prior $1.22B-$1.27B, driven by AI-powered CloudForge Platform adoption and enterprise net expansions.  

Subscription revenue, 94% of Q2, expected at $1.21B-$1.24B or 27-31% growth, backed by Q2-end ARR of $509 million (up 32% YoY) and trailing 12-month NRR of 118%. Large enterprise (> $1M ARR) at 125% NRR echoes Snowflake's AI phase. Pro services/other at $70M-$80M, up 15-25%, scaling Sentinel AI onboarding.  

Drivers: CloudForge Fusion AI suite for multi-cloud optimization, contributing 20% Q2 bookings, 40% upsell attach; zero-ETL pipelines halving time-to-value, Q3 AI agent previews targeting $500M TAM expansion. Added 45 net customers to 1,850 total, enterprise +28% YoY; $15M ARR bank win, Fortune 50 retailer expansions at 35%; <3% enterprise churn, 98% renewals, sales productivity +15% QoQ.  

Regionally: Americas (72% Q2 rev) 28-32% growth via AWS/Azure, US federal +60% post-FedRAMP. EMEA (18%) 35%+ with DACH finance wins. APAC (10%) 40% via Japan/Australia sovereignty, doubled headcount to 50, $10M Singapore telco. Embeds macro caution, $50M FX headwind, but consumption pricing (40%) and NRR insulate; high end of SaaS curve like CrowdStrike, 75%+ non-GAAP margins at 28-30%, Rule of 60+. R&D ~35%, S&M 22%, FCF $300M+ (23% margin).  

Finally, our next quarter ARR guidance for Q3 FY2025 ending September 30. We're guiding to $528 million to $538 million at quarter-end, or 4% to 6% sequential growth from Q2's $509 million, and 32% to 35% YoY. This embeds momentum in a resilient SaaS market despite constrained IT budgets from rates and geopolitics.  

NRR expected 115% to 118%, up from Q2's 114%, with top 100 customers >120% via AI analytics, Snowflake-like scalability, VMware/Nutanix edge in multi-cloud post-Broadcom. New ACV bookings 25-30% of growth: 45-55 logos at $450K avg ACV—highest in three quarters—via PLG self-serve trials in Slack/Teams like HubSpot for devops. Large wins include two Q2 eight-figure deals ramping, like Fortune 50 telco AWS-to-Azure.  

Churn/contraction under 3% annualized gross retention via ForgeGuard ML flagging risks 90 days early, shaving 150 bps YoY, outperforming ServiceNow in finance/healthcare. North America 65% bookings growth, EMEA 20% with GDPR AI for German banks, APAC 15% via Alibaba/NTT amid yen volatility, early LatAm Brazil fintech like Nubank.  

Investing $25M S&M to double field in cybersecurity observability vs. Databricks, R&D 22% for zero-ETL/composable AI lifting win rates 18%. Monitoring RFP delays, but 80% margins flex. Positions for $2.2B FY2025 ARR run-rate, toward 40%+ CAGR on AI; Rule of 50 at 85 shows leverage.  

We are updating our full-year guidance accordingly.  

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa for a technology update.  

Lisa Wong:  
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, like Fusion AI and Copilot, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes, with penetration rates over 28% and upsell economics adding substantial ARR. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers, including zero-ETL pipelines, edge computing for APAC sovereignty, and Sentinel for zero-trust, all while maintaining FedRAMP compliance and GDPR readiness. These innovations not only boost NRR but position us to capture the expanding multi-cloud management TAM.  

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.  

Operator:  
Thank you. To ask a question, press star one one. Our first question comes from Ben Thompson with Goldman Sachs.  

Ben Thompson:  
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of CloudForge AI Copilot on your overall growth, and what kind of attach rates are you seeing with it?  

David Kim:  
Thanks, Ben. The CloudForge AI Copilot has been transformative for our growth, contributing over 20% of new bookings in Q2 and accelerating our land-and-expand flywheel. It's driving expansions across our base, particularly in enterprise, where it's adding predictive analytics and workflow automation that stick at 95% renewal rates. Overall impact on revenue growth is significant, embedding about 10% into our raised FY2025 guidance through higher ACV and cohort NRR north of 120% in adopters. Attach rates are strong at 40% among eligible customers, exceeding our internal targets, with even higher 50%+ in top accounts integrating it with security suites. We're seeing this propel sales productivity up 15% and win rates 18% in betas, positioning it as a key differentiator against peers.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.  

Emily Chen:  
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region?  

Sarah Chen:  
Great question, Emily. International expansion, especially APAC, is a priority as we diversify beyond North America. We're targeting 40% YoY growth there, building on our 10% mix of Q2 revenue. Key plans include ramping partnerships with Alibaba Cloud and NTT to address data sovereignty and local needs, countering softer Japan demand from yen volatility. We've doubled APAC sales headcount to 50, secured a landmark $10M ARR telco deal in Singapore, and launched localized edge computing to boost expansion from 20 points. Early traction in LatAm pilots like Brazil fintech adds momentum. EMEA is also accelerating at 35%+ with GDPR AI wins in DACH banks. Overall, regions outside Americas will drive 30% of Q3 bookings growth, supporting our multi-cloud orchestration edge.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.  

Raj Patel:  
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, and what's the trend you are seeing in NRR?  

Mike Patel:  
Thanks, Raj. Churn management remains proactive amid macro pressures like budgets and inflation. We're at best-in-class 4.2% annualized dollar churn and 6.8% logo churn in Q2, down YoY, through 'Churn Fortress': expanded CS teams, ForgePredict ML at 88% accuracy rescuing 15% of risks, AutoPilot onboarding to 21 days, and FlexScale pricing stemming 18% budget churn. Win-back and renewals hit 94-98%. NRR trends up to 114% in Q2, guiding 115-118% Q3 on 25-27 point expansions from AI Copilot at 28-35% adoption. Trailing 118%, with FY25 to 120%+ as cohorts mature—well above peers, underscoring our sticky moat.  

Operator:  
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.  

Sarah Chen:  
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.  

Operator:  
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
